title: Calculate Capital Gains Before You Sell
meta_description: Calculate capital gains from proceeds, adjusted basis, losses and reliefs before selling shares, funds or property, then reserve cash and retain evidence.

sections.heading: Capital Gain Starts With a Disposal, Not a Rising Screen
paragraphs: The opening photograph shows a person calculating beside a live market chart. The chart can show an investment rising, but tax usually begins with a defined event and jurisdiction, not a green line. A capital gain is broadly the amount by which disposal value exceeds recognised cost after the rules allow specific adjustments.

Separate three numbers: current value, proceeds and taxable gain. Current value is an estimate before sale. Proceeds are what the transaction produces before or after specified costs. Taxable gain follows legal rules for basis, allowable expenses, reliefs, losses, currency and exemptions. They are rarely identical.

A gain can be unrealised while the asset is held and realised when it is sold, exchanged, gifted or otherwise disposed of under local rules. Some transactions trigger tax without much cash arriving, so never assume liquidity and liability occur together.

Write the asset, owner, residence, account, acquisition date, intended transaction and expected completion date before calculating. Capital-gains treatment depends on facts. A personal home, listed share, fund, cryptoasset and business interest can follow different rules even when the economic profit looks similar.

Tax applies to the owner recognised by law, not whoever enters the trade. Joint ownership, trusts, companies, spouses and nominees require documentation. Do not move ownership shortly before sale based on a social-media tip; transfers can create legal, tax and anti-avoidance issues.

This article teaches a calculation and evidence process, not a tax rate. Verify current official rules and seek qualified advice before a material or cross-border disposal. The right question is not ‘What percentage do I pay?’ but ‘Which rules apply to this exact transaction, and can every input be proved?’

Use a four-column fact sheet labelled fact, evidence, uncertainty and action. For example, the expected sale price is an estimate supported by a quote, while acquisition cost is a historical fact supported by a confirmation. This prevents a precise-looking spreadsheet from hiding assumptions. Mark who will resolve each uncertainty and by when. If the transaction changes, preserve the earlier version rather than overwriting it; the audit trail explains why the final decision differed from the initial plan.

sections.heading: Build the Gain Equation From Documents
paragraphs: Start with gross consideration: cash, property, debt assumed or other value received according to the applicable rule. Then identify transaction costs the jurisdiction permits, such as specified broker commissions, legal fees or transfer costs. Everyday ownership expenses may not be deductible from the gain.

Establish adjusted basis or allowable cost. It can begin with purchase price and include permitted acquisition costs or capital improvements, then change for prior depreciation, distributions, returns of capital, corporate actions or other adjustments. The broker’s displayed cost may be incomplete.

Do not treat maintenance as improvement automatically. A repair that restores condition may be an ordinary expense, while an enhancement can affect basis under specific rules. Preserve invoices, dates, descriptions and proof of payment; a bank transfer without scope does not prove what work occurred.

Translate foreign-currency amounts as required on each relevant date. Converting only the final profit can be wrong because purchase cost and proceeds may use different exchange rates. Keep the official or accepted rate source and method.

Calculate each disposal before applying losses, exemptions or rates. This keeps the asset-level evidence separate from return-level aggregation. A clean worksheet should let another person move from contract and statement to the reported number.

Reconcile the worksheet to cash without forcing them to match. Loan payoff, escrow, withheld tax and nondeductible selling costs can reduce cash received without reducing gain by the same amount. Explain every difference in a closing bridge.

Test basis independently. Rebuild it from source documents, then compare that amount with the broker or adviser record. Investigate every variance: transferred holdings, reinvested distributions, return of capital, foreign currency and reorganisations commonly explain gaps. Where a rule allows an expense, retain both evidence that it was paid and evidence of its connection to acquisition, improvement or disposal. A clean total with missing support is weaker than a well-indexed calculation showing each permitted component.

sections.heading: Identify the Tax Event Before Choosing a Date
paragraphs: A sale is the obvious disposal, but exchanges, gifts, deemed sales, fund distributions, options, reorganisations, worthless securities and asset transfers can produce different events. The trade date, contract date, completion date or distribution date used for tax depends on the rule and asset.

For securities, do not assume cash settlement date determines the tax year. The U.S. [[S1|IRS Topic 409]] and [[S2|Publication 550]] explain federal capital gain and investment-income concepts; transaction documents and current instructions remain necessary.

For property, binding contract and completion rules can differ by jurisdiction and facts. Record offer, exchange, completion and possession dates. A year-end closing can cross reporting periods when one date slips.

Gifts can be disposals at market value under some systems even when no money changes hands. Transfers between spouses may receive special treatment, but residence, separation and timing can matter. Verify before signing.

Fund investors may receive capital-gain distributions without selling units. Reinvesting a distribution can still create taxable income while adding new basis. Record both the taxable distribution and reinvested acquisition to avoid paying twice later.

Create an event memo before execution: action, asset, parties, expected tax date, valuation method, cash received and rule source. If any field is unclear, pause the transaction rather than reverse-engineering it during filing.

Distinguish a legal disposal from an operational instruction. A limit order can remain open, fill partly or execute over multiple days; a property agreement can be amended or fail to complete. Record the actual event after it occurs. For non-cash consideration, document how fair value was established and whether liabilities formed part of consideration. This post-execution check prevents an abandoned plan or estimated amount from being reported as though it were the completed transaction.

sections.heading: Property Gains Need Their Own Evidence File
paragraphs: The midpoint photograph shows a house key changing hands. It makes property disposal visible, but a key does not establish taxable gain. Purchase documents, ownership, residence use, improvements, selling costs, depreciation and relief conditions do.

Build a property chronology from acquisition through sale. Record purchase allocation, legal and transfer costs, dates occupied as a main home, rental or business periods, major improvements, refinancing and final selling expenses. Mortgage principal is financing, not automatically tax basis.

In the United States, [[S3|IRS Publication 523]] explains federal rules for selling a home, including ownership and use tests, exclusions and reporting. Rental depreciation can affect the result even when a home-sale exclusion applies to other gain.

In the UK, [[S6|HMRC guidance on Capital Gains Tax when selling property]] covers Private Residence Relief and property reporting. Residence periods, letting, grounds and use can change relief; do not assume every home sale is exempt.

Obtain valuations when required for a gift, inheritance, part-business use or historic transition. A retrospective estimate years later is harder and costlier to defend. Keep the valuer’s credentials, assumptions and effective date.

Reconcile the closing statement line by line. Estate-agent fee, legal fee, transfer tax, mortgage payoff, repairs and staging do not all receive identical treatment. Classify each item under the applicable rule rather than calling the entire closing deduction.

For mixed-use property, draw a simple timeline by month or year showing main-home, vacant, rental and business periods. Attach evidence such as utility records, leases and tax returns without assuming that one item proves residence. If land, fixtures or contents are included, verify whether values must be allocated. Agreeing an artificial allocation with a buyer does not necessarily bind the tax authority; obtain a defensible valuation when the split materially changes treatment.

sections.heading: Holding Period Changes Classification, Not Economic Profit
paragraphs: A £10,000 or $10,000 economic gain remains the same before tax, but holding period can change rate or classification. Record acquisition and disposal dates from documents and apply the jurisdiction’s counting rule.

U.S. federal rules distinguish short-term and long-term gains, with short-term net gains generally taxed using ordinary-income rates and long-term gains under separate schedules. Additional taxes, state rules and special asset rates may apply.
The UK does not use the same general short-term versus long-term rate system. Rates can depend on income, asset and tax year. Importing an American one-year rule into UK planning is a category error.

Do not hold a deteriorating investment solely to cross a tax date. Compare expected tax saved with market risk, concentration and the reason for selling. Tax is one transaction cost, not the investment thesis.
Likewise, avoid selling only because a lower rate seems available without checking taxable income, other gains, losses and benefit interactions. Rate bands can fill across the year.
Record alternative dates and uncertainty before executing. A deliberate timing choice has a quantified tax effect and a risk statement; a guess based on an internet headline does not.

Model timing with two complete tax-year scenarios rather than multiplying the gain by headline rates. Include other taxable income, expected distributions, deductions, losses, exemptions and additional taxes in each scenario. Then add a non-tax column for price volatility and concentration. This makes the trade-off visible: a projected tax reduction is not certain profit, while remaining exposed to an asset can produce gains or losses far larger than the estimated saving.

sections.heading: Losses Are Assets With Rules and Deadlines
paragraphs: Capital losses can offset gains under jurisdiction-specific ordering, limits and carry rules. A portfolio decline alone is not a realised loss. The transaction, evidence and timing must qualify.

In the United States, netting generally separates short- and long-term items before combining, and limits apply to deducting net capital loss against other income. Unused amounts may carry forward under federal rules.

The wash-sale rule can defer a loss when substantially identical securities are acquired within the relevant window. Check transactions across the investor and relevant accounts; automation in one brokerage may not see the household’s full activity.

UK share matching can connect a disposal with same-day acquisitions, acquisitions within the following 30 days and the Section 104 holding. HMRC’s [[S7|share-identification guidance]] should be applied before assuming a sale and repurchase crystallises the intended loss.

A loss is not valuable enough to justify an unsuitable trade. Estimate the usable tax benefit, transaction costs, time out of market, replacement exposure and portfolio effect. A loss carried for years may be worth less than its face amount today.

Maintain a loss ledger with origin year, character, amount used, amount carried and supporting return. Do not rely only on the latest broker statement because transfers and prior returns can alter the available figure.

Check whether a loss is economically permanent or merely deferred. A disallowed current loss may increase the replacement asset’s basis under some rules, while other restrictions can produce a different result. Document the adjustment and carry it into the new record. Also distinguish investment capital loss from theft, casualty, business or worthless-asset claims; labels used in everyday speech do not establish the tax category, timing or evidence standard.

sections.heading: Share Lots Can Produce Different Gains From the Same Sale
paragraphs: When identical shares were bought at different prices, the lot selected can alter gain, holding period and remaining basis. Average cost, first-in-first-out and specific identification rules differ by asset and jurisdiction.

Before a U.S. trade, verify the broker’s default method and whether specific identification is available. Obtain timely written confirmation of the selected lot. A preference entered after settlement may not change the tax record.

For UK pooled holdings, do not impose U.S. lot selection on the Section 104 pool. Apply statutory matching in order. Keep acquisition quantities, costs and corporate actions sufficient to maintain the pool.

Compare lot choices with portfolio policy. Selling the highest-cost lot may reduce current gain but leave a concentrated low-basis position. A larger current tax bill can sometimes support better risk reduction or future flexibility.

Coordinate charitable gifts and sales cautiously. Donating appreciated assets may receive special treatment when conditions are met, but valuation, eligible recipient, ownership and deduction limits matter. Do not sell first if the intended strategy requires an in-kind gift.
Record quantity sold, lot or pool rule, cost, date, proceeds, fees and confirmation. Reconcile after execution because partial fills and adjustments can change the intended outcome.

Run a remaining-basis test after every partial sale. Opening quantity and cost, disposals, acquisitions, adjustments and closing quantity should reconcile exactly. Rounding can accumulate across reinvestments and pooled holdings, so preserve sufficient precision and apply the required rounding only at reporting. If the custodian’s confirmation conflicts with the instruction, raise it promptly. The tax return should follow the legally effective transaction, supported by records, rather than the investor’s unexecuted preference.

sections.heading: Tax Wrappers Change Whether the Gain Is Currently Taxable
paragraphs: A sale inside a pension, retirement account or other tax-advantaged wrapper may not create an immediate capital-gains bill, but contributions, withdrawals and prohibited transactions follow separate rules. Account tax treatment is not the same as asset risk.

Identify the legal account before calculating. A brokerage interface may display taxable and retirement accounts together. Export each transaction with account title so a sale is not reported twice or omitted.

In the UK, disposals inside an ISA are generally treated differently from taxable accounts, while pension withdrawals follow pension rules. In the U.S., traditional and Roth retirement accounts defer or alter taxation under their own requirements.

Do not move assets into a wrapper merely to erase an existing gain without checking contribution limits and transfer rules. Many accounts accept cash contributions rather than in-kind transfers, so selling can still realise tax outside.

Asset location should consider income, turnover, foreign withholding, access and future withdrawal tax, not capital gains alone. The most tax-efficient account can be wrong for money needed before access age.
Maintain a master account map with owner, jurisdiction, wrapper, custodian and tax-report source. Review when moving country or consolidating providers.

Separate three decisions that are often blurred: which asset belongs in which account, whether to sell it, and whether to withdraw money. A sale inside a wrapper may be sheltered while a later withdrawal is taxable; the reverse can also occur under different account rules. Beneficiary designations and inherited accounts add further constraints. Model the complete path from contribution or acquisition to withdrawal instead of stopping at the absence of a capital-gains line today.

sections.heading: Residence and Currency Can Change the Entire Calculation
paragraphs: Tax residence, domicile or citizenship can determine which country taxes a gain. Asset location, treaty and departure or arrival dates can add reporting or credits. A broker’s location does not settle residence.

Cross-border movers should model sale before departure, after arrival and after any special holding period. Exit taxes, rebasing, temporary non-residence and foreign-tax-credit rules may apply. Professional advice before moving is more useful than repair after the transaction.

Keep purchase cost in original currency and the reporting-currency calculation required by each authority. Currency movement can create a taxable gain even when the asset price is flat locally, or reduce taxable gain despite a local profit.
Foreign funds can have reporting classifications that alter income and gain treatment. Verify the exact fund and share class, not merely the investment strategy.
Treaty relief is not automatic in every filing system. Preserve foreign tax paid, authority, date, income or gain type and conversion. A credit may be limited or claimed in a different period.
Create a residence memo for the sale year: days, homes, work, ties, citizenship, arrival and departure, and advice received. Do not put sensitive identity numbers in an exposed worksheet.

Cross-border advice should be coordinated rather than collected as two isolated answers. Give each adviser the same residence timeline, transaction facts and assumptions, then ask how double-tax relief and filing dates interact. One country may calculate the gain from original cost while another permits a rebased value, creating different taxable amounts. A treaty can allocate taxing rights yet still require disclosure. Capture unresolved differences in writing before choosing the sale date.

sections.heading: Gifts and Inheritance Transfer More Than an Asset
paragraphs: A gift can transfer basis or create a market-value disposal depending on jurisdiction and relationship. The recipient needs acquisition records even if the donor owes no immediate tax. Giving an asset without its history creates a future reporting problem.

Inherited assets may receive a new basis, probate value or another statutory treatment. Keep estate valuations, date of death, ownership documents and later improvement costs. Do not substitute the account value visible months later.
Compare gifting the asset with selling and gifting cash. The gain, deduction, recipient tax and control can differ. Include gift and inheritance tax regimes separately from capital gains.
Transfers to spouses or civil partners may receive special treatment, but separation, non-residence and later sale can matter. Document ownership proportions and effective date.
For trusts and companies, legal ownership and distributions can create tax at more than one level. Use advisers familiar with the entity and jurisdiction before transferring or selling.
Add a basis packet to estate planning: purchase confirmations, improvements, corporate actions, prior reliefs and tax returns. Beneficiary labels alone do not preserve cost history.

When receiving an asset, request a transfer statement containing the donor or estate’s acquisition data, relevant valuations, prior adjustments and the legal basis for the treatment claimed. When giving one, provide the same packet securely. For jointly inherited property, document each owner’s share and any later unequal spending. Informal family understandings about who ‘really owns’ an asset can conflict with deeds, account registrations and tax reporting, so resolve title before disposal.

sections.heading: Estimate Tax Before the Sale, Then Reserve Cash
paragraphs: A gain does not have one universal rate. Estimate taxable income, gain categories, losses, exemptions, deductions and additional taxes for the whole year. The sale can move income into another band or affect benefits and surcharges.
Build low, expected and high estimates. Use current official rates and state, local or foreign rules. Keep the estimate date because legislation and inflation-linked thresholds change.

Set aside cash from proceeds rather than reinvesting everything. Estimated-payment or advance-reporting deadlines can occur before the annual return. A tax reserve should remain liquid and separate from the emergency fund.

In the U.S., federal estimated-tax safe-harbour and withholding rules can affect penalties. Increasing wage withholding may differ operationally from making an estimated payment. Confirm with current IRS instructions or an adviser.
UK property disposals can have separate reporting and payment timelines. Verify whether the transaction falls within the current property service rules even when an annual return will also be filed.
Reconcile the final return with the estimate. Record why the result changed—other income, rates, losses, fees or valuation—so the next sale model improves.

Treat the reserve as a range, not an invitation to spend the lower estimate. Start with the high reasonable case, identify when missing forms or year-end income will narrow it, and release surplus only after reconciliation. If withholding or estimated payments are adjusted, retain the calculation and confirmation. Penalty rules can depend on timing, not merely total paid by year end, so a correct annual estimate does not automatically prove that instalments were sufficient.

sections.heading: Keep a Basis File That Survives Broker Changes
paragraphs: The late photograph shows a calculator, tax checklist and rate table. It makes the reporting stage visible: tax preparation depends on evidence accumulated before filing, not memory after a broker account closes.

Store confirmations, annual statements, transfer records, reinvested distributions, returns of capital, splits, mergers, spin-offs and fees. Corporate actions can allocate one original cost across several new securities.

When transferring brokers, compare outgoing and incoming quantities and basis. Correct errors promptly with both institutions. A transferred number marked unknown should not become the accepted answer by default.

Keep property deeds, settlement statements, improvement invoices, depreciation schedules and valuation reports. Photographing a receipt is useful only if the image remains readable and linked to the asset.

Use a secure index with asset ID, date, document type and storage location. Avoid full account numbers in a casual spreadsheet. Encrypt sensitive files, back them up and define retention with professional guidance.
Archive the filed return, schedules, computation and payment proof together. Future losses, audits, estate administration and cross-border claims may depend on the old calculation.

Create document checksums or use a controlled archive so a statement can be shown to be unchanged. Name files consistently with date, asset and type, and maintain an index that does not expose sensitive identifiers. Test restoration from backup annually. If a provider offers records for only a limited period, schedule exports before access expires. Good retention is not indiscriminate hoarding: apply lawful retention advice and securely dispose of duplicate sensitive files when no longer needed.

sections.heading: Avoid Timing Tricks That Create Larger Problems
paragraphs: Do not sell in December solely to use an allowance without confirming trade date, settlement, matching rules and portfolio need. Year-end liquidity and holidays can complicate execution.

Avoid repurchasing mechanically after a loss. Wash-sale or share-matching rules may deny the intended treatment, and a substitute can change market exposure. Plan the replacement security and risk gap first.

Do not let tax lock-in preserve dangerous concentration. Compare tax cost with the loss a single company or property could create. A staged sale, hedge, charitable transfer or offsetting loss may help, but each adds rules and costs.

Do not sell before gathering basis merely because a platform shows an estimated gain. Correct basis can change quantity, timing and reserve. If records are unavailable, document reconstruction method and obtain advice.

Beware advice that promises to eliminate tax through secrecy, sham residence, artificial loss or ownership that does not change economic control. Legitimate planning uses disclosed facts and current law.
Use a cooling period for optional trades, but not when delay worsens an expiring deadline or severe portfolio risk. The pre-sale worksheet should state why timing matters.

Apply a claim-evidence-rule test to every proposed tactic. The claim might be ‘this sale creates a deductible loss’; the evidence is the executed trade and basis history; the rule includes matching, related-party and replacement-purchase restrictions. If any layer is missing, describe the result as uncertain, not guaranteed. Professional credentials also matter: confirm that the adviser is authorised for the relevant jurisdiction and that the written scope covers the transaction, not just annual return preparation.

sections.heading: Use a Pre-Sale Gate Before Clicking Confirm
paragraphs: Complete an identity block: asset, quantity, owner, account, tax residence, acquisition history and proposed disposal. Confirm the account and security because a wrong-account trade can be irreversible.
Complete the calculation block: expected proceeds, allowable transaction costs, adjusted basis, gain character, losses, exemption, estimated rate and cash reserve. Show source links and assumptions.
Complete the portfolio block: reason for sale, remaining exposure, replacement asset, concentration after sale and trading costs. Tax should not be the only column.
Complete the deadline block: tax date, estimated payment, property report, annual return, foreign credit and documents expected from brokers or closing agents. Add calendar reminders with an owner.

Use go, revise or obtain advice. Advice is especially important for cross-border moves, trusts, business sales, gifts, inheritance, prior depreciation, unclear basis or a transaction large enough to change financial security.

After execution, replace estimates with actual fills and statements, fund the reserve, update basis and archive evidence. Capital gains become understandable when every reported number traces to a transaction and every planning choice remains subordinate to the investment or life reason for selling.

Have a second person review high-value worksheets using a fixed sequence: confirm units and currency, recalculate arithmetic, inspect evidence links, challenge rule dates, test loss ordering and compare the planned result with cash. This is not a substitute for professional advice, but it catches transposed figures and duplicated costs. Sign and date the final checklist. If a material assumption changes between approval and execution, reopen the gate rather than relying on the old sign-off.

Finally, write a transaction memorandum in language. State what was sold, why it was sold, how proceeds and adjusted basis were established, which losses or reliefs were applied, how much cash was reserved and which deadlines remain. Attach the calculation version used for the decision and link each figure to evidence. Note jurisdiction and tax year beside every rule rather than presenting rates or allowances as permanent. If an adviser prepared part of the work, record the question asked, information supplied, conclusion received and any limitation in scope. Review the memorandum when forms arrive because an information return can differ from the investor’s records without automatically being correct. Resolve differences before filing, document amendments and keep proof of submission and payment. This narrative turns a collection of statements into an understandable file for the taxpayer, reviewer, executor or future adviser. It also exposes unresolved assumptions while there is still time to obtain documents, adjust the reserve or request advice instead of discovering a preventable gap after a deadline.

summary: Capital gain is not the rise visible on a screen. Separate current value, proceeds and taxable gain. Start with the exact asset, owner, account, residence, acquisition and disposal because different transactions and jurisdictions follow different rules.

Build the equation from documents: consideration minus permitted transaction costs minus adjusted basis, followed by jurisdiction-specific losses, reliefs and exemptions. Basis can change through improvements, depreciation, distributions and corporate actions. Reconcile tax gain to cash without forcing them to match.

Identify the tax event and date before execution. Sales, exchanges, gifts, fund distributions, options and deemed disposals can differ. Create an event memo containing action, parties, valuation, expected tax date, cash and rule source.

Property needs a chronology covering purchase, occupation, rental or business use, improvements, depreciation, sale costs and relief. Mortgage payoff is financing, not automatically basis. Classify every closing item under the relevant rule.

Holding period can change classification or rate without changing economic profit. U.S. short- and long-term rules do not apply universally. Compare any timing benefit with market risk and the actual reason for selling.

Losses follow realisation, netting, use and carry rules. U.S. wash-sale and UK share-matching rules can defer or redirect losses. Maintain a loss ledger and never trade solely to create a deduction without evaluating replacement exposure and costs.

Share lots can produce different gains. Confirm the broker default and specific identification where allowed; apply statutory pooling where required. Record quantity, basis method, date, fees and execution confirmation.

Tax-advantaged wrappers can change current capital-gains treatment but create contribution, access and withdrawal rules. Keep an account map and do not assume assets can be transferred in kind without triggering a sale.

Cross-border residence, currency and fund classification can alter the calculation. Preserve original-currency records, residence dates, foreign tax and treaty evidence. Seek advice before moving or disposing, not after.

Gifts and inheritance transfer basis and evidence as well as assets. Keep valuations, ownership, improvement records and prior reliefs. Compare gifting an asset with selling and gifting cash under all relevant tax regimes.

Estimate the whole-year liability under low, expected and high cases, then reserve liquid cash. Check estimated-payment and property-reporting deadlines. Reconcile the final return with the estimate and explain changes.

Maintain a basis file through broker transfers and corporate actions. Store confirmations, distributions, splits, closing documents, invoices, depreciation and valuations securely. Archive the return, computation and payment proof together.

Avoid year-end, loss-harvesting or tax-avoidance tricks that ignore matching rules, deadlines or investment risk. Do not let a tax bill preserve dangerous concentration, and do not trade from an unverified estimated basis.

Before selling, complete identity, calculation, portfolio and deadline blocks. Use go, revise or obtain advice. After execution, replace estimates with actual amounts, fund the reserve, update basis and archive evidence.

Use a fact sheet that separates documented facts, assumptions, uncertainties and assigned actions. Rebuild basis independently and investigate differences with custodian data. For partial disposals, reconcile opening and closing quantity and cost so the remaining basis is as defensible as the reported gain.

Model timing with complete tax-year scenarios rather than a headline rate. Include income, gain categories, losses, reliefs and added taxes, then compare the projected saving with market and concentration risk. A lower estimated tax does not make an unsuitable investment decision suitable.

For a material transaction, have a qualified second reviewer check currency, arithmetic, evidence, current rule dates, loss ordering and cash reconciliation. Reopen the decision gate when facts change. The objective is not to eliminate every gain, but to sell for a sound reason with a traceable calculation, sufficient liquidity and timely reporting. Preserve that reasoning with the tax file.

faq.question: Is capital gain the same as sale proceeds?
faq.answer: No. Proceeds are value received. Gain generally compares recognised proceeds with adjusted basis and allowed costs before applying losses, reliefs and rates.

faq.question: Do I owe tax when an investment rises but I do not sell?
faq.answer: Often a market rise is unrealised, but fund distributions, deemed disposals and other events can create tax without a conventional sale. Check the exact transaction and jurisdiction.

faq.question: Does paying off a mortgage reduce property gain?
faq.answer: Mortgage payoff affects cash received but is generally financing, not automatically property basis. Purchase, improvement and selling-cost rules determine the gain calculation.

faq.question: Can I choose which shares I sell?
faq.answer: It depends. U.S. specific identification may be available with timely confirmation; UK pooled holdings follow statutory matching. Verify before trading.

faq.question: Can a capital loss always offset salary?
faq.answer: No. Ordering, annual limits and carry rules apply. The U.S. permits a limited net loss deduction against other income; other systems differ.

faq.question: Does moving country change capital-gains tax?
faq.answer: Potentially. Residence, citizenship, asset location, treaties, exit rules, rebasing and currency conversion can affect liability and reporting.

faq.question: What should happen immediately after a sale?
faq.answer: Replace estimates with actual fills or closing statements, reserve cash, update basis and loss ledgers, calendar deadlines and archive evidence.

glossary.definition: The taxable result from a disposal after applying recognised proceeds, basis, costs and relevant rules.
An increase in value while an asset remains held and no applicable realisation event has occurred.
A sale, exchange, gift or other event treated as ending or changing ownership for tax.
Recognised cost after permitted additions and reductions.
An expense the applicable tax rule permits in calculating gain.
Selecting documented securities lots for a sale where rules and broker procedures allow.
A U.S. rule that can defer a loss after specified replacement purchases.
The pooled cost basis used for many UK share holdings after higher-priority matching rules.
Liquid cash set aside for the estimated liability and payment deadline.
Potential relief for qualifying tax paid to another jurisdiction, subject to rules and limits.
